scope.head: ac144ef4759d14570bf686e6a0e6b2983075fa9b
scope.review_type: read-only architecture preflight; not final independent implementation review
scope.source_changes_status_claim: The initial source snapshot was at baseline; later root-owned Phase 1 edits are in progress and outside this preflight.

recommendation.legacy_inventory_equipment: preserve Record<ItemId, number> and fixed sword/armor fields and semantics; no legacy conversion
recommendation.save_migration: native V1/V2 without reward gets a pure empty extension only after legacy validation; present reward is strict validated; malformed extension fails closed
recommendation.wolf_combat: independent encounterWolf API plus optional tagged inline combat.familyEncounter; preserve legacy encounter/dungeon/chief route; no reward.encounter second source of truth

findings.evidence: validBase builds its required-key template from createGame(); matches requires every template object key. Adding reward without removing it from the legacy template rejects all native V1/V2 saves lacking reward.
findings.recommendation: Remove life and reward from the legacy base template and validate/default reward separately; keep V1 life rules and current world comparisons intact.

findings.evidence: combatTurn currently routes all non-dungeon wins through threat reductions and checks MONSTERS[monsterId].boss to clear the single goblin crisis boss, reset warnings, and write goblin-chief memories.
findings.recommendation: Use a tagged family encounter combat variant and isolated resolver; never mark wolf family entries as legacy boss records or let their victory use goblin settlement effects.

findings.topic: journal is not a state-diff archive
findings.evidence: packCheckpoint serializes the full state, while PlayRecord stores only operation/time/message/events.
findings.recommendation: Keep reward in GameState checkpoint; emit readable reward events. Do not rely on PlayRecord to reconstruct exact instances, stack counts, or discovery state.

findings.evidence: InventoryWindow and actions use ItemId stacks; transferStorage accepts ItemId and ownership storage validates the current ITEM registry; fixed sword/armor effects are read directly in combat.
findings.recommendation: Keep new material IDs and instances in reward state and the UI as a distinct projection; share only the existing weapon/armor slots and prevent dual effects.

reward.nextInstanceId: positive safe integer greater than every stored ID; never reused
reward.instances: unique ItemInstance records with ownerId, baseId, rarity, rolledStats, affixes, specialTrait, optional provenance
reward.materialsByCharacter: sparse character-keyed registry ID to nonnegative safe integer map
reward.equippedByCharacter: sparse character-keyed {weapon, armor} refs to owned, matching-slot instances
reward.collection: unique arrays of finite registered monster/item/material/boss IDs; each array length bounded by catalog size

combat.legacy: existing combat shape and action path unchanged
combat.familyEncounter: tagged optional inline metadata: definition/family, rank, variant, traits, turn/phase state, and resolved snapshot needed for deterministic load continuation
save_invariants: wolf base and family definition agree
resolved combat stats match saved encounter snapshot

verification.limitations: Source inspection only; no implementation existed at the reviewed HEAD.
